detail.title: Average Prices
detail.abstract: Average transaction prices collected by surveys, assessments or secondary data often serve as price benchmarks in markets that lack centralized exchanges. This paper examines when and how average prices facilitate eective price discovery. To do so we investigate a dynamic economic model that centers the coordinating role of the average price as a common reference price. We derive conditions for local price discovery and optimal price revision rates. The model provides sucient structure to estimate structural model parameters, including transaction price revision rates and implied market prot margins using only transaction price data. In a case study we estimate the model on transaction price data on Norwegian farmed salmon exports. We document frequent price revisions (average monthly rate of about 69%), signicant pricing agreement, and estimated buyer and seller prot margins consistent with industry data. The paper highlights the crucial role of Price Reporting Agencies (PRA) in determining the accuracy, eciency, and informativeness of price measures in decentralized markets.

detail.title: Reason for Treason

publicationDetails.detailsText: Centre for Quantitative History (CQH) Working Paper No. 16
publicationDetails.journalName: Centre for Quantitative History Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Defections during war are extreme changes in loyalty. What motivates military officers to betray their motherland and serve the invaders? Using a novel dataset of career paths for over 2,800 high-ranking (colonels and generals) Nationalist (KMT) military officers during the Second Sino-Japanese War (as part of World War II), we examine defection cases to Japanese puppet regimes. Three findings emerge. First, high-ranking KMT officers who advanced more slowly in their careers were more likely to defect; suggesting that internal organizational recognition matters. Second, officers who were underpromoted compared to their schoolmates and townsmen were more likely to defect, suggesting that peer comparison matters. Third, officers were more likely to defect when their defected peers had better career prospects in the enemy’s camp, suggesting that external recognition matters.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether merchant organizations shaped the wartime redistribution of political resources in late imperial China. During the Taiping Rebellion (1851–1864), the Qing government turned to merchant networks for war finance and, in exchange, expanded examination quotas for the shengyuan degree. Using crosssectional data on 262 prefectures, I show that pre-war merchant guild presence strongly predicts wartime quota increases, concentrated in battle-affected areas. Instrumenting guild presence with Ming-dynasty trade routes supports a causal interpretation. The lijin commercial tax is a plausible channel: prefectures collecting more lijin revenue received larger quota allocations. A difference-in-differences analysis confirms that quota expansions translated into higher jinshi production after 1864. The findings provide quantified evidence that fiscal contributions can purchase political selection in a premodern autocracy.

title: Security Issuance with Undersubscription Risk *
affiliations: Stanford Graduate School of Business and

detail.title: Security Issuance with Undersubscription Risk *
detail.abstract: A successful security issuance raises more capital and creates a more liquid aftermarket. This creates a coordination problem: undersubscription makes the security less valuable, weakening the incentive to subscribe. To ensure a successful offering, the issuance must be underpriced. Debt is the optimal monotone security as it minimizes underpricing. In equity offerings, underpricing is lessened by two common devices: ex-post share rationing and a minimum sales requirement.

title: Optimal Subsidy Targeting with Pigouvian, Ramsey, and Equity Objectives

detail.title: Optimal Subsidy Targeting with Pigouvian, Ramsey, and Equity Objectives
detail.abstract: This paper examines the design of corrective subsidies for positive externalities in a setting often observed in actual programs, where subsidy eligibility and amounts can be differentiated across market segments defined by recipients' observable and hard-to-manipulate characteristics, such as income and location. We develop a unified framework to optimally target or differentiate subsidy rates across these segments by decomposing each segment's optimal subsidy into three components aligned with the policy objectives—Pigouvian (externality correction), Ramsey (cost-effectiveness), and redistribution. The relative significance of these three components depends on the shadow value of the subsidy budget. We investigate how optimal subsidy targeting is influenced by market and policy primitives such as the program budget, the magnitude of positive externalities, production costs, heterogeneity across segments in responsiveness to subsidies and in social welfare weights. Overall, this paper provides a theoretically grounded and empirically implementable framework for designing differentiated corrective subsidies, thereby complementing the existing positive literature on the efficiency and distributional impacts of corrective subsidies. By integrating Pigouvian, Ramsey, and equity perspectives within a single optimal policy design problem, the paper bridges the theory of optimal taxes and subsidies, applied welfare analysis, and real-world policy design.

detail.abstract:
The accelerating deployment of generative AI systems-including large language models, synthetic media generators, and autonomous agents-has exposed a widening gap between the capabilities of deployed AI and the regulatory frameworks designed to govern them. Existing legislative instruments, including the EU AI Act (2024), the UK AI Regulatory Framework, and comparable instruments in the United States, were conceived against a landscape of narrower, more predictable AI applications. They are now being applied to systems that are probabilistic, emergent, opaque, and capable of operating autonomously across jurisdictions-properties for which static, compliance-based regulatory architectures are poorly suited. 

This paper presents a comparative analysis of current regulatory frameworks for three categories of AI system that present acute governance challenges: (1) generative synthetic media systems capable of producing deepfakes and AI-generated audiovisual content at scale; (2) large language model-based autonomous agents operating across multi-step, multi-platform workflows with limited human oversight; and (3) retrievalaugmented generation (RAG) systems deployed in high-stakes public interest contexts. Drawing on doctrinal legal analysis, comparative regulatory methodology, and practitioner experience, the paper identifies three structural governance failures common across jurisdictions, and proposes an adaptive governance model built on continuous compliance mechanisms, jurisdiction-sensitive risk tiering, and mandatory transparency obligations.

detail.abstract: Housing price distortion is typically analyzed through the lenses of affordability, finance, and distribution. While these perspectives are important, they do not fully capture the broader implications of housing systems for the structure of economic life. In particular, relatively little attention is given to the spatial consequences of sustained housing price escalation. This paper argues that housing markets must be understood not only as mechanisms that price shelter, but as systems that allocate access to space. Because economic activity is spatially concentrated, access to housing is also access to opportunity. As a result, the structure of housing prices plays a central role in determining how households are distributed across cities and how efficiently economic activity is organized. The paper develops a conceptual framework linking housing price distortion to spatial misallocation. It shows that when housing prices are shaped by financial demand, scarcity capitalization, and institutional constraints, they cease to function as reliable signals of productive location value. Instead, they become mechanisms that restrict access to high-opportunity areas. This shift generates a range of spatial distortions, including displacement from productive locations, increased commuting, and inefficient urban expansion. These outcomes have cumulative effects on labor allocation, infrastructure demand, environmental pressure, and aggregate productivity. The paper contributes by integrating housing price dynamics with spatial economic outcomes and introduces Paxpacte as a framework for evaluating housing systems in terms of how they structure access to space and opportunity.

title: Colonialism as if the Colonized Matter:  Professor Acemoglu and the Ainu
affiliations: Harvard Law School

detail.title: Colonialism as if the Colonized Matter:  Professor Acemoglu and the Ainu

publicationDetails.detailsText: An earlier version of this article appeared as SSRN 5584031.  The article has been published as Independent Law Journal, 1: 153 (2026).

detail.abstract:
Acemoglu, Johnson & Robinson posit that colonizing countries promoted growth in places where their citizens planned to live by introducing rational economic and legal institutions.  By contrast, where they faced high mortality rates, they introduced only "extractive" legal institutions.  They took what they could and left.  The former places thrived; the latter failed.

                        All this attributes economic performance to the colonizers rather than the colonized.  Less tactfully, it denies the colonized (whether the indigenous groups in the U.S., the Inuit to the north, the Australian aboriginals -- or the Japanese Ainu), their agency.  Disproportionately, Acemoglu, et al.'s countries with high settler mortality rates were places that had only recently made the transition from hunter-gatherer economies to settled agriculture, if they had made it at all.  Unlike agriculturalists, hunter-gatherers generally lack a sense of private ownership over the most obvious capital asset -- land.  Without legal title to that capital asset, they have little reason to defer gratification and invest in it.  For the most part, they also fight each other at rates generally unseen among agricultural societies.  With no tradition of legal ownership or long-term investments in land, but with chronic and lethal violence, Acemoglu, et al.'s high-mortality-rate communities would not have been able effectively to exploit rational legal institutions anyway.

                        I illustrate (only illustrate; I do not claim to prove) this intuition with an example outside of the (perhaps excessively debated) range of Canada, the U.S., or Australia.  Instead, I take the example of the Japanese Ainu.  As of the mid-19th century, most Japanese lived either in settled agricultural communities or in booming commercial cities.  The hunter-gatherer Ainu, however, lived in the northern-most island of Hokkaido.  When the Japanese government introduced western legal institutions at the turn of the century, it applied the new rules both to the agricultural and commercial regions outside of Hokkaido and to the hunter-gatherer communities within Hokkaido.  Over most of Japan, men and women quickly learned to exploit the opportunities presented by the new legal system.  In Hokkaido, the Ainu failed to do any of that.  Contrary to the stories told by western scholars who try so hard to shut down discussion of failure among indigenous groups, the Ainu  simply intermarried with the other Japanese and disappeared.  The innovation and investment that would eventually transform Hokkaido came instead with immigrants from the rest of Japan.

title: Volatility Forecasting with Machine Learning: A Horse Race Across GARCH, HAR, and Tree-Based Models
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Volatility Forecasting with Machine Learning: A Horse Race Across GARCH, HAR, and Tree-Based Models
detail.abstract: We run a controlled horse race between seven volatility forecasting model configurations on S&P 500 realized volatility from January 2004 through November 2025: three GARCH variants (GARCH, EGARCH, GJR-GARCH), the HAR-RV model of Corsi (2009), gradient-boosted trees (LightGBM, XGBoost), and an equal-weight ensemble of LightGBM, HAR-RV, and GARCH(1,1). All models are evaluated on the same data, the same features, and the same expanding-window protocol over a January 2022 to November 2025 test period (980 trading days) that spans the 2022 bear market, the 2023 rally, the 2024-2025 rate normalization, and a 19.4% drawdown year. We use QLIKE as the primary loss function alongside RMSE and Mincer-Zarnowitz R-squared, and report Diebold-Mariano two-sided p-values for all key pairs. Three findings emerge. First, on the full test sample, GJR-GARCH is the best individual model (QLIKE 0.3447) and the equal-weight ensemble narrowly leads overall (QLIKE 0.3431), but the ensemble's edge over GJR-GARCH is not statistically significant (p = 0.90). Second, the full-sample ranking masks a substantial subperiod reversal: in 2022, the GARCH family wins (EGARCH best at QLIKE 0.2346), while LightGBM ranks last; in 2023-2025, tree models lead and HAR-RV is last. The 2022 environment is structurally different from the calm 2019-2021 validation period that drove early stopping, so parametric GARCH adapts more gracefully than the 35-feature trees. Third, the LightGBM split-importance ranking shows that VIX is the dominant feature, the leverage effect is captured through three different return-based features that together account for roughly 19% of split count, and long-horizon RV signals dominate over short-horizon ones. We release the full LaTeX source, the data-collection and modeling scripts, the per-day forecasts of all seven models, and the supplementary metrics under permissive licenses, scoring 2 on the Reproducibility Disclosure Score rubric of Khan (2026).

title: Transaction Data, Payment Services, and Bank Competition in Open Banking
affiliations: University of Saskatchewan - Economics

detail.title: Transaction Data, Payment Services, and Bank Competition in Open Banking
detail.abstract: Open banking reallocates customer data, but those data are often created by payment services. We study that trade-off in a dynamic model of payments and credit in which banks generate borrower-specific transaction records by processing payments. Portability intensifies screened-lending competition, yet lets rival banks free-ride on information created by the payment bank, weakening incentives to generate data. Estimated on Brazilian public data, the model implies a small pre-reform outright-credit segment and positive welfare effects of portability conditional on active payment provision. Untargeted validation supports reallocation toward working-capital lending during the rollout period. Per-transaction compensation dominates access fees and privacy frictions.

title: Geopolitical Instrumentalization Theory (GIT)

detail.title: Geopolitical Instrumentalization Theory (GIT)
detail.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive theoretical introduction to Geopolitical Instrumentalization Theory (GIT), a framework developed through a series of four research papers published between August 2025 and February 2026. GIT addresses a structural gap in mainstream international relations theory: the capacity of hegemonic powers to exploit the dynamics of ostensibly adversarial projects in ways that systematically serve their strategic objectiveswithout requiring direct coordination or conspiracy.

title: Financial security and stability of the US banking system: comparative analysis and parallels with the Ukrainian experience («Financial security»)

detail.title: Financial security and stability of the US banking system: comparative analysis and parallels with the Ukrainian experience («Financial security»)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study does not involve human participants or personal data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This study develops an integrated risk-based model for assessing the financial security and stability of banking systems, using the United States as a benchmark and drawing comparative parallels with the Ukrainian banking sector. The research combines Basel III/IV, CAMELS, SREP, capital adequacy, liquidity, asset quality, market risk, operational risk, and managerial resilience indicators into a unified analytical framework. The proposed model supports supervisory assessment, internal risk management, and systemic stability monitoring. A distinctive contribution of the study is the introduction of a managerial resilience coefficient linking human resource stability, professional qualifications of risk-management personnel, and operational losses. The model contributes to financial system resilience, macroprudential supervision, and institutional risk governance, with direct relevance to the US banking system.

title: A Theory of Groupality: Decisive Foundation, New Classification System, Three Drives, and Ontological Structure — A New Unit Concept for 21st Century Social Science

detail.title: A Theory of Groupality: Decisive Foundation, New Classification System, Three Drives, and Ontological Structure — A New Unit Concept for 21st Century Social Science
detail.abstract: Personality, refers to a collective entity capable of response, memory, and self-persistence, yet structurally incapable of singular legal responsibility. Corporations, political parties, religious organizations, capital systems, media cartels, and platforms are all instances of groupality. The paper makes three decisive contributions. First, it proposes a new classification system: the binary classification of Pae-pa (覇派, Hegemonic Faction) and Min-pa (民派, Civic Faction), with Mega Agent (including PAG, Pure Absence Groupality) as a separate category. This system academically diagnoses that the progressive-conservative and left-right paradigms have exhausted their utility as analytical instruments, and establishes a new framework for the 21st century. Second, it identifies the Three Drives of groupality—Self-Preservation, Expansion, and Justification—whose combinatorial patterns structurally determine action. Third, it establishes the ontological structure of groupality, drawing on East Asian operational ontology that decisively reinforces the BE-verb ontology of Western philosophy. The distinction between Pae-pa and Min-pa is not a distinction of ideology, but of whose desire is being represented. Pae-pa politically represents the desires of hegemonic groupalities; Min-pa spontaneously crystallizes the PFS (Paleolithic Fairness Sense) of civic groupalities. Mega Agent is a separate category—the individual who provides the face of a hegemonic groupality. CFG (Capital Finance Groupality) is treated as a decisive case of hegemonic groupality, not a category. This paper is the Foundational Theory of approximately 100 academic assets of the Simup Sasang Institute, including ULBP, ULRP, micro-deception theory, TPTS, Mito-Theory, and Min-pa Theory.

title: A Multi-Cloud Governance and Site Reliability Engineering Framework for FinTech Platforms: A Case Study

detail.title: A Multi-Cloud Governance and Site Reliability Engineering Framework for FinTech Platforms: A Case Study
detail.abstract: Financial technology (FinTech) platforms increasingly rely on multi-cloud architectures to achieve scalability, resilience, and vendor independence. However, this paradigm introduces significant challenges in governance, observability, and operational reliability. This paper presents a comprehensive Multi-Cloud Governance and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) framework tailored for FinTech environments. The proposed framework integrates governance policies, reliability engineering principles, and observability mechanisms into a unified architecture. A real-world case study demonstrates the effectiveness of the approach, achieving 99.99% availability, a 40% reduction in mean time to resolution (MTTR), and a 30% improvement in cost efficiency. The findings highlight the importance of standardized governance and SRE practices in enhancing the reliability and compliance of distributed financial systems.

title: Leptons as Complete Torsion Cycles

detail.title: Leptons as Complete Torsion Cycles
detail.abstract:
The Perceptual Vibrational Framework (PVF) proposes that charged leptons are not three independent static particles but three manifestations of the same torsion oscillation cycle at three amplitude levels. This paper presents three connected results. (1) Cycle picture: tau, muon, and electron correspond to maximum, intermediate, and turning-point configurations of a vacuum filament torsion cycle. (2) Entropy-mass duality: tau occupies the minimum entropy (maximum winding) configuration; the electron occupies the maximum entropy (zero-torsion turning point) configuration. The electron is interpretable as the thermodynamic fixed point of the muon cycle, which is consistent with its observed stability without invoking a new conservation law. (3) Geodesic drift correction: the moving center of the muon torsion cycle shifts the effective torsion amplitude by a factor (1 - 2r^4/lambda), giving the most precise lepton mass predictions in PVF.

 

Numerical results: m_mu = m_tau x r^2(1 + r^2/2)(1 - 2r^4/lambda) = 105.696 MeV (0.036% error). Via Koide Q=2/3: m_e = 0.5087 MeV (0.443% error). Both represent best-ever PVF predictions, with m_e improved 12x over v6. The geodesic drift coefficient is physically motivated but carries a residual 7% uncertainty and is labelled semi-derived.

m_mu: 0.036% error  |  m_e: 0.443% error  |  12x improvement over v6

This version directly addresses the five concerns raised in peer review of v7: (1) Entropy is now defined explicitly with a mathematical expression and numerical values. (2) The electron ontological claim is softened to an interpretation consistent with QED, not a replacement. (3) The geodesic drift term is labelled SEMI-DERIVED with its 7% coefficient gap stated honestly. (4) A tau lifetime order-of-magnitude estimate is added. (5) A Standard Model correspondence section is added. The core results and errors are unchanged from v7.

title: BRIEFING NOTE: CANADA'S OPTIONS IN THE DARFUR PHASE OF THE SUDANESE WAR

detail.title: BRIEFING NOTE: CANADA'S OPTIONS IN THE DARFUR PHASE OF THE SUDANESE WAR
detail.abstract:
Briefing Note here addresses the current human security concerns in Darfur
with a focus on policy options that Canada can pursue to both engage its role in
international peacebuilding and preserve important emerging international trade
opportunities. Drawing on the author’s direct experience in Darfur with the
United Nations and over three decades of work in war-affected contextsin Africa,
the Middle East, Latin America and Southeast Asia, this note avoids reiterating
the well-documented atrocities in Sudan and instead focuses on options that can
technically de-escalate the security problem in Darfur - the region of highest
humanitarian and security concern. It identifies three actionable technical levers:
1. disrupting conflict-gold supply chains, 2. reinforcing accountability signals
that can affect combatant behaviour, and 3. operationalizing Sudanese civil
society and diaspora-linked micro-peace mechanisms. Failure of the international
community to act in Darfur risksregional destabilization, famine, ongoing human
rights violations and the fragmentation of Sudan.

title: Measuring the Impact of AI on Productivity: Cross-Sectoral Evidence from Eighteen Economies Post-ChatGPT
affiliations: and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Measuring the Impact of AI on Productivity: Cross-Sectoral Evidence from Eighteen Economies Post-ChatGPT
detail.abstract: This paper measures the impact of artificial intelligence on aggregate productivity from observed sectoral outcomes. We use a panel difference-indifferences specification on U.S. sectoral productivity data through 2025Q4, with sectoral AI exposure measured by the Workflow Completeness construct (C *) validated against firm-reported adoption in companion work. We estimate that AI is contributing approximately $731 billion per year to U.S. trend productivity growth across five primary sector representing approximately 60 percent of GDP, with a 95 percent CI of [$413B, $1,048B], raising the 5-sector aggregate productivity growth rate to +5.3 percent per year against a +1.3 percent counterfactual. The result is statistically significant under every cluster-robust inference method we test, survives eight named alternative-mechanism tests. Extending the methodology to eighteen additional economies, we identify positive AI contributions of approximately $154 billion per year in the EU 12 pooled panel, $170 billion in China, and statistically significant individual contributions in six mid-sized economies; combined with the U.S., AI is contributing approximately $1.0 trillion per year to trend productivity across the United States, EU 12, and China, again on the same five-sector base covering roughly 60 percent of GDP in each economy.

title: Interjecting unilateral Indian GAAR inquiries in cross-border setting: Revisiting tax normativism post Tiger Global
affiliations: Supreme Court of India

detail.title: Interjecting unilateral Indian GAAR inquiries in cross-border setting: Revisiting tax normativism post Tiger Global
detail.abstract:
It is not an overstatement to christen the recent decision of Supreme Court of India in the Tiger Global case as a watershed moment in India's international tax paradigm. While there are many facets of the decision, this article is concerned with the declaration qua Tax Residency Certificates [TRC] issued under the bilateral tax treaties and the conclusions that inter alia (a) TRC alone is not sufficient to avail the benefits under the tax treaties, and (b) TRC is not binding on any statutory authority or Court unless the authority or Court enquires into it and comes to its own independent conclusion. Citing the GAAR provisions, the Supreme Court has further held that it is incumbent upon the taxpayer to "furnish sufficient material" that the transaction was not "designed with the sole intent of evading tax". 

Respecting the constitutional stipulations that the decision is the law of the land,  this article attempts an inquiry whether the incumbent legal position represents a normative equilibrium. It is argued that from a normative standpoint there is merit in the approach to accord a greater role to foreign 'competent authority' [CA] even while conducting GAAR inquiries in cross-border setting, especially in those cases which can result into denial of tax treaty benefits.

title: What Moves Meaning? Investigating Drivers of an Idiosyncratic Incentive

detail.title: What Moves Meaning? Investigating Drivers of an Idiosyncratic Incentive

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no competing interests to declare.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This design was approved by the Institutional Review Board (IRB) at UC Davis - Protocol # 2225085-2.
declarations.funderStatement: Funding for this experiment received from UC Davis Department of Economics Graduate Research Award and 2025 Bacon Family Summer Fellowship.

detail.abstract: I develop a novel online experiment with 488 participants on Prolific to examine how two interventions, an information treatment emphasizing the social importance of a task and a generative treatment prompting workers to reflect on what they personally find meaningful, affect perceptions of work meaningfulness. While the information treatment increases meaningfulness for the intended prosocial task by 7%, it also raises reported difficulty by 20% overall. In contrast, the generative treatment increases meaningfulness for some workers without affecting perceived difficulty. Examining attenuation of these effects, reported meaningfulness declines approximately 2% at endline for those in the information treatment, while those in the generative treatment show no such decline. Together, these findings suggest that generative approaches may offer a more desirable pathway to work meaningfulness, delivering more durable gains without increasing perceived difficulty.

title: Supreme Court on Redistribution of Community Resources: Realizing Dr. Ambedkar’s Vision of Economic Justice
affiliations: Supreme Court of India and Advocate, Supreme Court of India

detail.title: Supreme Court on Redistribution of Community Resources: Realizing Dr. Ambedkar’s Vision of Economic Justice
detail.abstract:
Addressing a decades old controversy surrounding the true purport and contours of Directive Principles enshrined in the Constitution, a 9-judge bench of the Supreme Court of India in Property Owners’ Case exposited and vindicated the State’s entitlement to redistribute the ownership and control of the material resources of the community to subserve larger common good. The decision traces the ideas of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar to conclude that a welfare state, which India is, presupposes such egalitarian outlook. 

In this backdrop, this article seeks to juxtapose the recent Supreme Court’s decision with Dr. Ambedkar’s ideas towards effectuating economic justice for the resource-less and downtrodden members of the society. Expanding the coverage further, this article examines specific ideas and political expressions of Dr. Ambedkar and various decision of Supreme Court which are inspired by him, to expand the economic justice theory mooted by Dr. Ambedkar and its overwhelming influence on contemporary India.

Chapter published in Prof. (Dr.) Vijay Kumar Singh (Ed.), Economic Justice And Public Finance For Social Change: An Appraisal in the light of Dr. Ambedkar's Vision (Satyam Law International) (April 2026) [ISBN: 978-8119122103]

title: National Impact Velocity (NIV): Catching Preliminary Systematic Stress Before Recessions
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: National Impact Velocity (NIV): Catching Preliminary Systematic Stress Before Recessions

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This research relies exclusively on publicly available, anonymized aggregate macroeconomic time series from the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) database. No human or animal subjects were involved.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant or financial support from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. All work was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: National Impact Velocity (NIV) is a parsimonious macroeconomic indicator designed to detect systematic stress accumulation before recessions by measuring the velocity of regenerative capital formation against cumulative economic friction. The framework synthesizes investment dynamics, monetary liquidity, capacity utilization, and credit circulation inhibitors into a single composite signal. Validated through six out-of-sample tests spanning 504 months (1970–2024), NIV achieves an out-of-sample AUC of 0.8538 at the 18-month horizon, filters 98.5% of false alarms via an L2-regularized ensemble, and contributes 41.71% orthogonal variance beyond the Federal Reserve 10Y–3M yield spread. Across the three major modern systematic crises in the validation window, the framework flags onset with an average lead time of approximately 5.3 months and identifies thrust-channel deterioration as the dominant trigger in five of six pre-contraction windows. The full code, data pipeline, and an interactive dashboard are publicly available at regenerationism.ai and github.com/direncode, with all experiments reproducible from the FRED API.

title: Digital Payments, Financial Inclusion and Rural Development in India: Evidence from UPI Adoption
affiliations: Late. Mansaramji Padole Arts College Ganeshapur Bhandara

detail.title: Digital Payments, Financial Inclusion and Rural Development in India: Evidence from UPI Adoption
detail.abstract: Digital payment technologies have significantly transformed financial systems across emerging economies. In India, the rapid expansion of the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has reshaped payment infrastructure and expanded access to financial services. Introduced by the National Payments Corporation of India under the supervision of the Reserve Bank of India, UPI has enabled seamless real-time transactions between bank accounts through mobile devices. This study examines the relationship between digital payment adoption, financial inclusion, and rural development in India during the period 2016-2024. Using secondary data from official financial databases and national payment statistics, the research applies panel regression models and diagnostic tests to evaluate the impact of UPI transaction growth on rural income and financial access indicators. The results indicate that digital payment expansion is significantly associated with improvements in financial accessibility and rural economic outcomes. The findings highlight the role of digital payment infrastructure in promoting inclusive economic growth and strengthening financial ecosystems in developing economies.

reference: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19711769
title: Restructuring TVET Bioscience Education for the Bioeconomy: A Concept Paper from Kenya with Lessons for Africa

detail.title: Restructuring TVET Bioscience Education for the Bioeconomy: A Concept Paper from Kenya with Lessons for Africa
detail.abstract: Kenya, like many African countries, faces a critical mismatch between Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) bioscience education and the emerging bioeconomy. A KNQA tracer study found that only 22% of Applied Biology graduates were employed within two years. Concurrently, Kenya's bioeconomy is estimated to contribute over 15% to GDP by 2030, yet lacks a skilled workforce in areas such as biopesticides, waste valorization, biofuels, biomaterials, conservation enterprises, and upstream circular economy principles (designing out waste, material passports, component harvesting). This concept paper proposes the restructuring of the Diploma in Applied Biology into a competency-based, stackable Diploma in Bioeconomy Technology and Entrepreneurship (DBTE). The program integrates Greening TVET, CBET, dual training, entrepreneurship incubation, and modular micro-credentials. It includes a "Bioeconomy Bridge" pathway to retool past graduates, rectifying a past policy failure. The DBTE is designed as a replicable model for other African countries. This paper uses Kenya as a case study, with lessons applicable across Africa, and aligns with the African Circular Economy Alliance (ACEA) framework.

title: AI in Financial Reporting
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: AI in Financial Reporting
detail.abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is fundamentally transforming financial reporting, offering unprecedented opportunities to overcome the inefficiencies, costs, and error vulnerabilities inherent in traditional manual systems. Utilizing a qualitative methodology based on a systematic thematic review of secondary academic and industry literature, this study investigates the impact of AI technologies-specifically machine learning, natural language processing, and data analytics-on corporate reporting practices. The findings reveal a significant upward trajectory in corporate AI adoption between 2018 and 2024. Organizations utilizing these technologies report substantial improvements, including accelerated reporting cycles, enhanced data accuracy, and superior capabilities in fraud detection and predictive forecasting. Despite these quantifiable benefits, the research highlights critical ongoing challenges such as data quality dependence, algorithmic opacity (the "black box" effect), and cybersecurity risks. Ultimately, this paper concludes that while AI serves as a powerful catalyst for operational efficiency and analytical depth, it is not a substitute for human expertise. To ensure the reliability and integrity of financial disclosures, AI must be deployed as a complementary tool, firmly guided by professional judgment, ethical oversight, and robust regulatory frameworks.

title: When Does Coordination Matter? Large-scale Evidence On Structural Contingencies In The Team Player Effect
affiliations: Business Administration & Economics, , Business Administration & Economics, Business Administration & Economics, Business Administration & Economics and Business Administration & Economics

detail.title: When Does Coordination Matter? Large-scale Evidence On Structural Contingencies In The Team Player Effect

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: The value of being a "team player" is not fixed – it depends on how work is organized. Using 1.5 million matches among 30,459 players in temporary teams formed by quasi-random matchmaking, we measure each player's coordination ability as a stable trait distinct from solo technical skill. This "team player effect" has a standardized coefficient ratio to individual skill (TPE/SELO) of about 47% in team contests but near zero in solo play. The return to coordination is strongly context-dependent: across a team-size × task-structure grid, the TPE/SELO coefficient ratio shifts from 35% to 72% (2.1×; 1.28×–1.49× within player), driven by team scale increasing coordination demands and task interdependence attenuating the predictive power of individual skill. Teammates perceive this quality, re-selecting high-coordination partners 23% more often. These findings connect individual coordination capabilities to organization design, providing field-scale evidence for classical contingency theory's prediction that the value of coordination depends on structural context.

title: Gendered and Environmental Impacts of Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen, Jal Jeevan Mission, and UJALA: Evidence from Villages in Bihar and Odisha

detail.title: Gendered and Environmental Impacts of Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen, Jal Jeevan Mission, and UJALA: Evidence from Villages in Bihar and Odisha
detail.abstract: Rural development schemes in India have increasingly aimed to improve the quality of life by expanding access to sanitation, safe drinking water, and electricity. However, the gendered and environmental dimensions of these interventions remain underexplored. This study examines the impact of three major government initiatives such as the Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM), Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), and the UJALA Scheme on women’s lives in selected villages of Bihar and Odisha. The research focuses on how these schemes have influenced women’s access to essential services, time use, safety, health, environmental conditions, and participation in household decision-making. Using a mixed-methods approach that includes household surveys, interviews, and field observations, the study documents women’s experiences in Pilkhi and Nekpur villages in Bihar, and Belgachia and Naranpur villages in Odisha. The findings indicate that while these schemes have significantly improved infrastructure coverage, important gaps remain in usage, awareness, maintenance, and inclusion. Access to household toilets and piped water has reduced the physical burden on women and contributed to improvements in hygiene and environmental cleanliness. However, many women continue to report limited involvement in household decision-making related to sanitation, water use, and resource management. In addition, caste and economic inequalities continue to shape how benefits from these schemes are distributed. Although the UJALA Scheme improved household lighting and enhanced perceptions of safety, its impact on women’s economic participation and empowerment remains limited. The study suggests that infrastructure provision alone does not guarantee gender equity or environmental sustainability. Women’s needs, voices, and participation must be integrated into the planning, delivery, and monitoring of rural development programmes. The findings highlight the importance of addressing intersectional factors such as caste, class, and spatial location in shaping development outcomes. A more gender-responsive and community-driven approach is necessary to ensure that rural infrastructure policies contribute not only to improved services but also to long term social, environmental, and economic empowerment.

reference: CESifo Working Paper No. 12629
title: The Impact of Trade Wars on Firms in Third Countries
affiliations: Bank of Italy, , Bank of Italy, Bank of Italy and Bank of Italy

detail.title: The Impact of Trade Wars on Firms in Third Countries

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Bilateral trade shocks affect firms in third countries by redirecting demand and reallocating competition across markets, creating winners and losers. We propose a tractable trade model with heterogeneous firms to decompose firm-level export responses as a function of destination-specific changes in demand, own-price and cross-price elasticities, and external economies of scale. Using the 2018–2019 US-China trade war as a source of exogenous variation and data on the universe of Italian firms, we show how bilateral trade shocks occurring elsewhere identify these primitives for third countries. On average, the US-China trade war created a 2.5% export gain, albeit with substantial heterogeneity across firms. The external economies of scale channel accounts for three-quarters of changes in export performance.

title: A Cross-Country Comparison of the Spatial Distribution of Cash Access Points in Switzerland and France
affiliations: University of St.Gallen - Swiss Payment Behaviour Lab, University of St. Gallen, Télécom Paris and Paris Dauphine University

detail.title: A Cross-Country Comparison of the Spatial Distribution of Cash Access Points in Switzerland and France
detail.abstract: This report compares access to cash infrastructure in France and Switzerland using high-resolution population data and geolocated cash access points to assess travel distances and times by car in 2024. Despite differing demographic and administrative structures, both countries maintain high overall accessibility, with most residents reaching cash services within short distances. Switzerland demonstrates slightly better accessibility, particularly in rural areas, due to its more balanced settlement structure. France exhibits greater rural disparities, mitigated significantly by its extensive post office network. The findings underscore the importance of complementary infrastructures—ATMs, bank branches, and post offices—in ensuring near-universal cash access across diverse territorial contexts.

title: The aggregate implication of mergers and acquisitions in the banking sector *

detail.title: The aggregate implication of mergers and acquisitions in the banking sector *
detail.abstract: The data in the United States shows the pattern of assotative matching, where the characteristics of acquirer and target banks are similar. Why does this pattern arise, and what is the aggregate implication of M& A in the banking sector? To answer this question, I build a search model of bank merger which can explain the assortative matching. The numerical exercise shows that assymmetric synergy, where there is complementarity between the productivity of acquirer and target bank in determining productivity of a bank after merger. The model is used for counterfactual simulation of banking merger prohibition to see how the merger and acquisition is in the banking sector affects the aggregate economy. * The author wish to thank Dean Corbae, Enghin Atalay, Oliver Levine, and Wako Watanabe for helpful comments.

title: Swiss Payment Monitor 2026: How does Switzerland pay? Issue 1/2026 - Survey November 2025
affiliations: University of St.Gallen - Swiss Payment Behaviour Lab, , ZHAW School of Management and Law - Institute of Marketing Management and ZHAW School of Management and Law - Institute of Marketing Management

detail.title: Swiss Payment Monitor 2026: How does Switzerland pay? Issue 1/2026 - Survey November 2025
detail.abstract: This study presents findings from the 14th Swiss Payment Monitor, based on a representative online survey (n=1,616) and a four-day payment diary (n=1,173) conducted in late 2025. Swiss payment behaviour shows increasing stabilisation after years of transformation, with mobile payments remaining dominant but entering a stagnation phase. Credit card usage increased significantly, particularly in transaction value, while debit cards remained most frequently used. Cash usage continued to decline, both in transaction share and average wallet holdings. Twint maintained market leadership among mobile providers, neobank adoption reached record levels, and payment security perceptions proved highly context-dependent, balancing convenience with situational trust concerns.

reference: CESifo Working Paper No. 12628
title: Delayed Retirement: Effects on Health and Healthcare Utilization
affiliations: Aarhus University, Aarhus University, Aarhus University and Aarhus University

detail.title: Delayed Retirement: Effects on Health and Healthcare Utilization

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: We estimate the impact of an increase in the early retirement age (ERA) on labor supply, health, and healthcare use using a regression discontinuity design. Raising the ERA increased employment and use of public transfers. Effects on GP visits and painkiller use are precisely estimated, small, and insignificant, while antidepressant and cardiovascular drug use increased slightly, but only borderline significantly. Those induced to work had lower pre-reform income and wealth, whereas those not working despite exposure had poorer pre-reform health. We argue that possibilities for exiting employment serve as a mitigating mechanism by sorting vulnerable individuals out of employment.

title: Navigating impressions: Topic-specific and structural design choices in CSR reports
affiliations: Technische Universitat Berlin and

detail.title: Navigating impressions: Topic-specific and structural design choices in CSR reports

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: This study examines topic-specific and structural impression management (IM) in CSR reports. Specifically, we analyze whether or not IM techniques are symmetrical across environmental, social, and governance subtopics, and how structural design characteristics reflect opportunism. Using a sample of 4,627 CSR reports issued by S&P 1500 firms, our results show managerial behaviors to purposefully shape the design of environmental and social subtopics to improve the perception of ESG performance. In contrast, managers rather withhold governance subtopics when governance performance is poor, suggesting that IM is topic-specific and not generalizable to the entire document. In addition, we find that managers strategically structure CSR reports through positional features and discretionarily select the quantity and weighting of ESG subtopics. Specifically, we find a lower readability, higher positivity, and higher colorfulness in the initial report partition relative to the remainder, likely because managers focus IM on the beginning, which mainly affects stakeholder reactions. Finally, our results show a positive relationship between the quantity and weighting of environmental, social, and governance subtopics and the associated performance, indicating that managers emphasize favorable information to convey a positive firm image.

title: Prenatal and childhood exposure to common plasticizers and risk-taking behavior in young adolescents
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, New York University (NYU) - Grossman School of Medicine, New York University (NYU) - Grossman School of Medicine, New York University (NYU) - Grossman School of Medicine, Erasmus University Rotterdam (EUR) - Department of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry, Government of the United States of America - National Institute of Mental Health and Erasmus University Rotterdam (EUR) - Education & Child Studies

detail.title: Prenatal and childhood exposure to common plasticizers and risk-taking behavior in young adolescents
detail.abstract: BackgroundEmerging evidence suggests endocrine disrupting chemicals, including bisphenols and phthalates, may affect behavioral development in children and adolescents. Risk behavior constitutes a potentially sex hormone sensitive behavioral construct. Here, we examined longitudinal associations of phthalate and bisphenol exposure with performance-based tasks and self-reported risk-taking behaviors.MethodsWithin a population-based birth cohort in the Netherlands, urinary bisphenols and phthalate metabolite concentrations were measured in women during pregnancy (three times, n=1379) and in children (once at 6 years, n=775). At 10 years, child risk-taking behavior was assessed with the computerized experimental Columbia Card Task (CCT). At 14 years, adolescents completed a computerized self-assessment of real-life risk-taking behaviors. Linear regression and hurdle models adjusted for confounders were applied in the whole sample and stratified by sex at birth.ResultsIn girls, prenatal mono-isobutyl phthalate was associated with a higher average CCT-score, indicting more risk-taking (B per 10-fold increase in creatinine-adjusted average prenatal levels= 2.10, 95% CI: 0.68,3.51). In boys, higher prenatal and childhood mono-[(2-carboxymethyl)hexyl] phthalate levels were associated with a higher CCT-score (prenatal B=6.21, 95% CI: 1.57,10.47; childhood B=6.02, 95% CI: 1.57,10.47). No associations were observed for bisphenol exposure nor for self-reported risk-taking.ConclusionsPrenatal phthalate exposure was associated with more risk-taking in an experimental task at 10 years-of-age, with sex-specific differences. The task reflects risky decision-making, which may be a hormonally sensitive construct. Risky decision making potentially precedes real-life risk-taking, which was captured by the self-reported measure and was limited in this young sample.

title: Rerouting of Chinese products in response to US trade tariffs: evidence from Italian firms’ expectations
affiliations: Bank of Italy

detail.title: Rerouting of Chinese products in response to US trade tariffs: evidence from Italian firms’ expectations

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 1000
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study how Italian firms perceive the potential rerouting of Chinese products, as a result of US trade restrictions, and its implications for prices, business conditions, investment and macroeconomic expectations. Using firm-level data from the Survey on Inflation and Growth Expectations, we show that while most firms do not anticipate a significant reallocation, a sizeable minority – around 30 per cent, concentrated among manufacturers and exporters – expect an increase in Chinese supply. Exposed firms foresee modest reductions in intermediate input prices and downward pressures on selling prices, particularly when competition is the dominant channel for transmitting the rerouting shock, while labour costs are found to exert upward pressures in some service sectors. The anticipated rerouting of Chinese products also generates long-term uncertainty about business conditions and dampens investment expectations. At the aggregate level, firms view the rerouting shock as denting short-term macroeconomic confidence, while leaving inflation expectations largely unchanged.

detail.title: Macroeconomic shocks and the term premium in the US

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Temi di Discussione (Working Paper) No. 1520
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the macroeconomic drivers of the US ten-year term premium using a daily Structural Vector Autoregressive model with sign and narrative restrictions, a framework that has not been previously applied in this context. Domestic uncertainty, inflation compensation, and domestic demand shocks explain most of the daily variation in the term premium. Domestic uncertainty, in particular, plays a central role, as it is the only shock that explains the strong negative co-movement between the expected short-term rate and the term premium, a stylized fact that has so far gone unnoticed in the literature. We use the model to revisit the behaviour of the term premium since the onset of the Great Financial Crisis, with a focus on more recent events where changes in the term premium have been at the centre of policy debate. Our results shed light on the quantitative relevance of specific channels and challenge existing narratives about these episodes.

title: Judgment Decay in AI-Augmented Environments: A Framework for Continuous Measurement and Embedded Maintenance of Human Decision-Making Capability
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Judgment Decay in AI-Augmented Environments: A Framework for Continuous Measurement and Embedded Maintenance of Human Decision-Making Capability

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of COHESION Research, which is developing tools related to the framework described in this paper. This relationship is disclosed for transparency.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper presents a theoretical framework. No human participants were involved and no empirical data were collected. Ethics approval was not required.

detail.abstract: AI decision-support systems are increasingly assuming cognitive tasks historically central to professional expertise across healthcare, aviation, criminal justice, and finance. While automation complacency has been studied for decades (Parasuraman & Manzey, 2010), and the fundamental paradox of automation was identified over forty years ago (Bainbridge, 1983), no integrated framework exists for continuously measuring, actively maintaining, and verifiably documenting the progressive deterioration of independent decision-making capability as it occurs across AI-augmented professional environments. This paper introduces the construct of Judgment Decay — the progressive, measurable deterioration of independent decision-making capability that occurs when professionals routinely defer to AI recommendations. I build on complacency research from aviation and automation, self-efficacy and autonomy theory from clinical psychology, situation awareness theory, and dual-process cognition to propose the Judgment Maintenance Framework — an integrated architecture with four components: (1) continuous measurement of judgment decay through AI interaction patterns, (2) invisible maintenance through clinically informed micro-interventions embedded within AI systems, (3) continuous verification via a composite Judgment Independence Score, and (4) embedded integration at the AI system level. The framework directly addresses the EU AI Act's mandate for "effective human oversight" (Article 14) by operationalizing a requirement that the regulation mandates but does not define. This paper makes three contributions. First, it introduces Judgment Decay as a formally defined construct distinct from automation complacency, automation bias, and skill atrophy, integrating these previously separate literatures under a unified clinical framework. Second, it proposes the Judgment Maintenance Framework grounded in self-efficacy theory, self-determination theory, and desirable difficulties research. Third, it operationalizes the EU AI Act's oversight mandate by providing measurable indicators and a composite Judgment Independence Score.

title: The public origins of American innovation

detail.title: The public origins of American innovation

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Temi di Discussione (Working Paper) No. 1521
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study the macroeconomic effects of government-funded and privately funded innovation on postwar US productivity and economic growth. Using newly digitized data that allow us to distinguish innovations by funding source and ownership, we document systematic differences in how public and private innovation translate into aggregate outcomes. Government-funded but privately owned patents—though accounting for only about 2 per cent of total patenting— explain roughly 20 per cent of medium-term fluctuations in total factor productivity and GDP growth and are associated with strong spillovers to business-sector R&D and investment. Privately funded patents also contribute to aggregate fluctuations, but with smaller effects, while publicly owned patents display muted average impacts despite being disproportionately represented among highly disruptive innovations, particularly in health and biotechnology. Across federal agencies, innovations funded by the NIH and NSF exhibit the strongest links to subsequent productivity growth, and research institutes and universities outperform for-profit firms in converting public funding into aggregate gains. Taken together, our results highlight how the institutional design of public support for innovation shapes medium-term productivity dynamics and plays a central role in sustaining US economic growth.

Това са нормативно закрепени основни ръководни начала, които изразяват най-важните идеи, върху които е изградена правната уредба на медиацията. title: Does Whistleblowing Improve Performance?

detail.title: Does Whistleblowing Improve Performance?
detail.abstract: Shareholder wealth is associated with company performance through better dividends. Good strategy, planning, and business ethics have an impact on company performance. This shows that the satisfaction of various parties with the company increases when performance increases. Rules, regulations, and laws must be strictly followed to increase the wealth of shareholders and other stakeholders. The presence of a whistle blower is considered important to align company objectives with shareholder objectives. Any wrongdoing can have a negative impact on the company's performance and stakeholders, as well as a negative reputation. The presence of whistleblowers is crucial in protecting the public's interest, avoiding expropriation, and curbing illegal activities.

detail.title: Labor productivity, effort and the euro-area business cycle

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Temi di Discussione (Working Paper) No. 1522
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Labor productivity is highly procyclical in the euro area. We investigate the sources of this procyclicality in an estimated New Keynesian business cycle model with labor search frictions and variable factor utilization in both capital and labor. Labor input can vary along three margins: employment, hours, and effort (or utilization). We find evidence for a significant use of the effort margin in labor adjustment. Moreover, a model that uses effort outperforms one with variable capital utilization or dominant technology shocks. Finally, the effort margin dampens inflation volatility.

title: Capital as a Viscous Fluid: A Navier-Stokes Framework for Modeling Sudden Stops and Flow Reversals in the Korean Financial Market

detail.title: Capital as a Viscous Fluid: A Navier-Stokes Framework for Modeling Sudden Stops and Flow Reversals in the Korean Financial Market
detail.abstract: This paper introduces a novel empirical framework that treats international capital flows as a viscous, incompressible fluid governed by a modified form of the Navier-Stokes equations. We rigorously map financial market variablesincluding market capitalization (fluid density, ρ), asset valuation multiples (pressure gradient, ∇p), trading volume-weighted price changes (flow velocity, u), market friction costs (kinematic viscosity, ν), and macroeconomic shocks (external force, f)-onto hydrodynamic parameters. Using the Korean KOSPI market as a primary laboratory, we provide empirical evidence from the March 2026 geopolitical crisis triggered by the U.S.-Israel-Iran military conflict, during which KOSPI suffered a two-day cumulative decline of 19.3% and witnessed a foreign capital outflow of approximately KRW 12 trillion (USD 8.7 billion), a Sudden Stop event of historic magnitude. We demonstrate that the fluid dynamics model successfully captures nonlinear capital flow dynamics-including turbulence, pressure-driven reversals, and viscosity-induced liquidity freezes-that traditional Vector Autoregression (VAR) models systematically fail to explain. In out-of-sample tests, our hydrodynamic model outperforms the VAR benchmark, reducing RMSE by approximately 38% in predicting flow reversals. [NEW] We further validate the framework through a computational implementation using a 1D finite difference Navier-Stokes solver applied to daily market data over the period 2020-2026. A regime-switching portfolio strategy derived from the model achieves a cumulative return of +132.2% (annualized 18.0%, Sharpe ratio 1.47) versus +56.7% for a passive 60/40 benchmark, while limiting maximum drawdown to-17.3% compared to-34.8% for a full-equity strategy. The direction prediction accuracy of the numerical solver reaches 99.4% with a correlation coefficient of 1.000 between predicted and actual flow velocities. We apply this framework to institutional pension fund ETF allocation strategies, proposing a VIX-regime-switching investment rule grounded in the external force term. Our findings contribute to both the econophysics literature and practical macroprudential policy design.

detail.title: Housing markets and the heterogeneous effects of monetary policy across the euro area

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Temi di Discussione (Working Paper) No. 1523

detail.abstract: This paper studies why monetary policy affects euro-area member states unevenly, focusing on three housing and mortgage market characteristics: homeownership rate, adjustable-rate mortgage share, and loan-to-value ratio. Using euro-area data, I show that higher values are associated with stronger consumption and mortgage rate responses. A two-country New Keynesian currency-union model with household heterogeneity reproduces observed heterogeneity and isolates three channels—cash-flow, homeownership rate, and mortgage credit—the last dominating. A Portugal case study shows amplification arises when all features are high. Closing Portugal’s gap relative to the euro-area average would require reducing its LTV ratio to roughly one-third of its current level, underscoring how limited this macroprudential instrument is for addressing monetary-policy heterogeneity on its own.

title: From Labor to Attention: A Token-Economic Framework for the AI Era

detail.title: From Labor to Attention: A Token-Economic Framework for the AI Era

declarations.funderStatement: The author is co-founder of cPen Network, a project exploring attention-based token systems.

detail.abstract: Modern economies distribute income and legitimacy primarily through labor. As AI and automation expand across cognitive, physical, and administrative work, that arrangement becomes more fragile (Frey and Osborne, 2017; Acemoglu, 2025; Eloundou et al., 2024). The same forces that weaken labor-centered income also increase the economic centrality of human attention: AI reduces the demand for human labor while increasing the supply of goods and content competing for finite human attention (Simon, 1971; Goldhaber, 1997). These two dynamics have been studied separately but not connected. This paper bridges that gap with three contributions. First, the Attention Triad distinguishes attention contribution, aggregation, and monetization as separate economic functions, making visible the contribution gap in current attention markets. Second, the attention-centered economy is proposed as a structural parallel to the labor-centered economy, arguing that the forces weakening labor-based inclusion simultaneously strengthen the case for attention-based compensation. Third, the Attention-Token Economic Model (ATEM) specifies a governance-conscious institutional framework for compensating verified human attention, illustrated through a tokenized architecture with revenue-backed sinks. A formal model identifies viability conditions including critical mass thresholds, and a sensitivity analysis demonstrates that viability is dominated by network effects. These mechanisms are presented as institutional design tools whose legitimacy depends on demanding conditions of privacy, proof-of-humanity, governance, and restraint.

affiliations: , Nakhchivan State University and Nakhchivan State University

detail.title: Digital Transformation of the TRIPP Route: Building Smart Logistics Ecosystems in the Zangezur Corridor
detail.abstract: The emergence of digital technologies has significantly transformed global logistics systems, particularly within strategic transit corridors. This study explores the digital transformation of the TRIPP (Trans-Regional Intelligent Physical Platform) route, focusing on the development of smart logistics ecosystems in the Zangezur Corridor. By integrating blockchain, artificial intelligence, and Industry 4.0 technologies, the research examines how digital infrastructure enhances efficiency, transparency, and sustainability in transit operations. The study employs a qualitative analytical approach based on recent academic literature to identify the key technological and economic drivers shaping modern logistics networks. The findings reveal that digital transformation not only improves operational performance but also redefines regional economic integration and geoeconomic dynamics. The paper contributes to the literature by proposing a conceptual framework for smart logistics ecosystems in emerging transit corridors.

reference: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 1003
title: Can GenAI fill banks’ emissions data gaps?
affiliations: Bank of Italy and Bank of Italy

detail.title: Can GenAI fill banks’ emissions data gaps?

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 1003
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper presents new evidence highlighting significant limitations in emissions data for major listed banks in the euro area, sourced from four leading providers. Notable issues are data gaps, inconsistencies across providers and high volatility over time in scope 3 emissions, which are often inexplicably lower than scope 2 emissions and do not correlate with the banks’ exposure to high-emitting sectors. The paper then examines whether Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), which relies on broader and diverse information sets, can help bridge the existing data gaps by comparing the outcomes from three GenAI tools. We find that GenAI-based emissions data, either estimated or retrieved, are correlated with data from traditional sources and may therefore help to partially fill current gaps and identify anomalies in the available data. Nevertheless, they suffer from similar issues in terms of quality and consistency to those documented for the data supplied by professional providers. Additional concerns regard replicability and transparency, underscoring the need for initial caution in their use. Despite the current limitations, looking forward, GenAI may become a valuable complementary data source as models that are fine-tuned for this task are developed. Future improvements will also depend on the availability of more reliable underlying information, which in turn requires parallel progress in defining simple, clear and actionable measurement standards as well as regulatory developments to promote climate disclosure by non-financial corporations within banks’ portfolios.

detail.title: Corporate lending by Italian less significant institutions: an empirical analysis

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 1004
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This study examines the reasons behind the higher default rates of loans granted by Italian banks categorized as less significant institutions (LSIs) under the Single Supervisory Mechanism compared with those issued by significant institutions (SIs). Using loan-level data matched with firm characteristics, the analysis shows that LSIs tend to serve smaller and riskier firms, which explains much of the observed default differential. After controlling for firm and loan characteristics, the remaining difference is substantially reduced. The pricing applied by LSIs appears broadly aligned with that of SIs, conditional on observable factors. These findings suggest that LSIs may facilitate access to credit for firms with potentially more limited financing opportunities.

reference: NBER Working Paper No. w35105
title: Trends in Health Inequalities among Spanish Retirees
affiliations: Spanish National Research Council (CSIC), Autonomous University of Barcelona, Erasmus University Rotterdam (EUR) - Erasmus School of Economics (ESE), Universitat Pompeu Fabra (UPF) and University of Barcelona

detail.title: Trends in Health Inequalities among Spanish Retirees

publicationDetails.journalName: NBER Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Spain, with one of the highest life expectancies globally and a rapidly ageing population, faces growing challenges in sustaining its pension, healthcare, and long-term care systems. This study examines trends in health inequalities among retired Spaniards from 2004 to 2022, using eight waves of the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE). We analyse five health outcomes—limitations in daily and instrumental activities, number of chronic conditions, a composite health deficiency index, mental health (EURO-D scale), and cognitive performance—and use linear regression to assess income-related gradients, adjusted for age and sex. We also compute a catch-up time measure—the number of years a poorer individual would need to reach the same level of health as a richer individual—and concentration indices of bad health. We then examine how these inequalities change over time, allowing us to explore the potential influence of pension reforms within the context of Spain’s Beveridge-style healthcare system and tax-funded long-term care provision. Our results show no clear evidence that health inequality has increased from 2004 to 2022. These findings contribute to understanding how income disparities interact with social protection systems in ageing societies and inform the design of equitable health, long-term care, and pension policies.

title: Time-Window Optimized Tracking of Mobile Numbers Using BTS Logs for Forensic Intelligence
affiliations: Rajalakshmi Institute of Technology (RIT), Chennai, Rajalakshmi Institute of Technology (RIT), Chennai, Rajalakshmi Institute of Technology (RIT), Chennai and Rajalakshmi Institute of Technology (RIT), Chennai

detail.title: Time-Window Optimized Tracking of Mobile Numbers Using BTS Logs for Forensic Intelligence
detail.abstract: This paper presents an enhanced Time-Window Optimized Tracking (TWOT) framework designed to improve forensic intelligence through automated analysis of Cell Tower Dump (BTS) data. Traditional investigative workflows rely heavily on manual inspection of large telecom datasets to identify mobile numbers present near multiple crime scenes, resulting in slow, labor-intensive, and error-prone analysis. The proposed TWOT system introduces an automated scoring methodology that evaluates each mobile number using three core metrics: Temporal Proximity, which measures the alignment of device activity with the incident time window; Spatial Proximity, which quantifies distance and occurrence frequency across towers near the incident location; and Frequency of Presence, which captures repeated tower connections within a buffered timeframe. To advance beyond conventional retrospective analysis, the framework incorporates a Predictive Presence Model that forecasts a device's likely future location using mobility-sequence learning, thereby enabling proactive suspicion estimation. These components are normalized and combined into a composite Suspicion Score that prioritizes potential persons of interest. The system is implemented using simulated BTS/CDR data and integrates geographical computation, time-series filtering, and machine-learning-based refinement. Experimental results demonstrate that the enhanced TWOT framework significantly reduces investigative effort while improving the speed, accuracy, and intelligence of digital crime-scene correlation. The approach provides a scalable, predictive, and data-driven enhancement to current forensic practices, with strong potential for real-world deployment by law-enforcement agencies.

title: Linking Multiple Taxation to Price Instability in Nigeria: A Quantitative Analysis of Challenges of Agricultural SMEs in Lagos State.
affiliations: University of Oxford

detail.title: Linking Multiple Taxation to Price Instability in Nigeria: A Quantitative Analysis of Challenges of Agricultural SMEs in Lagos State.
detail.abstract: This study analyses how exposure to multiple taxes influences instability in prices charged by SMEs in the agricultural markets of Lagos. It theoretically explains how weak institutions can support multiple taxation thereby leading to price instability in agricultural markets. This study collected primary data from 90 agro-SME owners at Ketu and Mile 12 markets in Lagos State. It adopts a positivist philosophy to vet the link between multiple taxation and price instability. It confirms that 74 agro-SME owners strongly acknowledge that multiple taxation impacts price instability in the agricultural markets of Lagos. This study concludes that multiple taxation has a negative effect on price stability in the agricultural markets of Lagos. It also concludes that business uncertainties in the agricultural markets of Lagos State are worsened by a poor tax collection system. This study recommends that proper fiscal policies should be implemented to establish a single tax window that enables agro-SMEs to ensure price stability in the agricultural markets.

title: Tracing AI Assistance and AI Agents in Survey Research
affiliations: and

detail.title: Tracing AI Assistance and AI Agents in Survey Research
detail.abstract: Generative AI creates a measurement problem for survey research. When respondents can outsource summarization, explanation, or fact retrieval, open-ended answers may no longer reflect their own reasoning. We introduce an auditable toolkit that combines response-process paradata with prompt-specific semantic benchmarks to detect AI use in open-ended responses. We validate the approach in a randomized survey experiment in which participants complete a summary task under either blocked AI access or observed access to an embedded AI tool, and by administering the same instrument to a synthetic AI agent. AI-assisted and automated responses leave distinct behavioral and textual traces: they show reduced drafting and revision, greater similarity to AI benchmark output, and lower distinctiveness relative to peer responses. Classifiers built on these signals achieve strong out-of-sample performance. These findings show that, in the age of generative AI, authorship must be measured rather than assumed.

title: Artificial intelligence and the US economy: an accounting perspective on investment and production

detail.title: Artificial intelligence and the US economy: an accounting perspective on investment and production

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 1006
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved to the centre of policy, market and academic debates, but its macroeconomic footprint is still only partly understood. This paper provides an overview on how the reverberations of the AI wave are captured in US national accounts, combining a simple macro-accounting framework with a stylized description of the AI production process. We highlight the crucial role played by data centres, which constitute the backbone of the AI ecosystem and attracted formidable investment in 2025 to meet the worldwide demand for AI services. In the first three quarters of the year, the boom in IT and AI-related capital expenditure clearly boosted aggregate US demand; the contribution to GDP was more limited, as a result of the high import incidence in AI hardware. Furthermore, simple calculations suggest that, at current utilization rates and pricing, the production of services originating in new AI data centres could boost GDP in the near future on a scale comparable to that recorded so far by investment spending. Short reinvestment cycles and uncertainty about future AI demand, while yet to act as a drag on growth, can nevertheless fuel macroeconomic risks over the medium term.

reference: NBER Working Paper No. w35106
title: China's Global Ownership
affiliations: Georgetown University - McDonough School of Business, European Central Bank (ECB),  and

detail.title: China's Global Ownership

publicationDetails.journalName: NBER Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
We study the global footprint and real effects of Chinese overseas corporate ownership. By assembling a comprehensive micro-level dataset of 161,773 firms across 159 countries (2012–2021), we independently reconstruct multi-layered ownership chains to trace capital through offshore tax havens to its ultimate origin. This approach reveals a global footprint substantially broader than official FDI statistics. Chinese-controlled foreign assets expanded at 20% annually, reaching $2.1 trillion or roughly 3% of global corporate assets by 2021. Chinese investors—particularly state-owned enterprises (SOEs)—strategically target R&D-intensive and supply-chain-linked firms. Following acquisition, target firms increase capital stock and R&D expenditures, yet these inputs fail to generate higher patent output and are accompanied by a significant decline in profitability. We document a novel 'innovation spillback' mechanism: while target innovation remains stagnant, Chinese parent firms experience a sharp acceleration in granted patents following their first developed-economy acquisition. Furthermore, a greater Chinese presence crowds out R&D at non-target peer firms, though aggregate industry-level innovation remains unchanged. China thus represents a distinctively state-driven model of global ownership that accepts weaker near-term performance to internalize technological capacity at home.
